To transcribe, your audio is sent to OpenRouter and to the model you choose; your key pays only for what you use.

OpenRouter brings together models from several companies with a single key and a single balance: you pay only for what you use, with no subscription.

What's sent: recording doesn't use the internet, and the audio stays on your phone until you transcribe it. When you transcribe, the audio (and your known voices, if you separate speakers) goes to OpenRouter and to the model you choose. For the note, only the transcript text is sent.

“Automatic” uses the model Verbapp recommends. The model list updates itself from OpenRouter once a day: new ones show up as “New · untested” and, if OpenRouter retires the one you use, Automatic switches to the next one on its own.

The model with speakers is used when you separate speakers (Person 1, Person 2…); the text-only one, when you don't.

Note AI: you choose a family (Claude, GPT or Gemini) and OpenRouter always uses its newest version. Each note shows which one wrote it.

Hourly prices come from the OpenRouter list and are a reference: OpenRouter reports the actual charge for each transcription.

Try them one at a time. Each recording\'s details show which ones were used.

Each option does something different:

• Record with the phone's noise reduction: uses the microphone mode for calls, the one that cleans up noise when you talk on the phone. It works very well with one person close to the phone, but it can turn down people who speak from farther away (in a meeting, for example), and every brand does it its own way. It applies to new recordings.

• Remove hum and level the volume: before sending to transcribe, it removes the low sounds that aren't voice (engine, air conditioning, bumps) and evens out the volume so quiet or distant voices come up.

• Reduce background noise (experimental): before sending, it lowers steady noise, like a fan or traffic. It's gentle on purpose: a strong filter can also affect the voice.

• Enhance voices when listening: it only changes how recordings sound in Verbapp's player.

The last three never change your recording: they work on a copy. To compare, transcribe the same recording again (“Transcribe again…”) with an option on, then with it off.
